top_signals.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
top_signals.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows.

top_signals.title: DayOne Is Said to Pause US IPO Plans on Data Center, Market Concerns
top_signals.summary: DayOne Data Centers Ltd. has put plans for its multibillion-dollar US initial public offering on hold, people familiar with the matter said, as investors question the sustainability of frothy valuations for digital infrastructure supporting the artificial intelligence boom.

top_signals.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Houthi Attacks Reignite Middle East Supply Fears
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices earlier today reversed a decline that began earlier in the week, gaining on reports of fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi targets and continued tanker trouble in the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $92.67 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was changing hands for $83.06 per barrel, after media reported the Yemeni Houthis had struck targets in Riyadh, including the city’s financial district and the headquarters of the country’s sovereign wealth fund, as well as a petrochemicals company…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Refineries have shifted production away from gasoline to middle distillates
top_signals.summary: Particularly high refinery margins for distillate fuel oil and jet fuel have contributed to shifts in the refinery yields of major products in 2026. Data from our latest Petroleum Supply Monthly—which includes data through August 2026—indicate refinery yields of gasoline have decreased significantly this year to support increased production of distillate fuel oil and jet fuel, sometimes referred to as middle distillates due to their relative cut points in the oil refining process.
